title: Cache & CDN Advanced
description: Cache-key, origin, and edge processing differences.

attacks.name: Cache key normalization
attacks.desc: Differing normalization of query parameters or paths can make a cache store one response under the wrong key.
attacks.prevention: Define cache keys from the canonical request path, query, and relevant headers used by the origin.

attacks.name: Unkeyed header poisoning
attacks.desc: A header omitted from the cache key can poison a response served to later visitors.
attacks.prevention: Include security-relevant headers in the cache key or ignore them before origin routing; do not cache tainted responses.

attacks.name: Fat GET poisoning
attacks.desc: Some caches ignore GET bodies while an origin processes them, creating a response-key mismatch.
attacks.prevention: Reject request bodies on GET where unsupported, and keep proxy and origin cache semantics aligned.

attacks.name: Cache deception
attacks.desc: A dynamic private page may be cached as a static-looking path and served to another visitor.

attacks.name: Vary header abuse
attacks.desc: Missing Vary directives can cause responses for one origin or content variant to be reused for another.

attacks.name: CDN origin bypass
attacks.desc: Direct requests to an origin can bypass CDN or WAF rules if the origin accepts public traffic.

attacks.name: Edge-side include injection
attacks.desc: Unsafe edge-side include processing can interpret attacker-controlled markup as an include directive.

attacks.name: Cache poisoning via cookies
attacks.desc: If a response changes with a cookie that is not in the cache key, one user's content may reach another.
